localContext: Mount Prospect homes, especially the 1950s–60s brick ranches and split-levels, often have original steel garage doors. These single-skin, un-insulated doors are common in areas like Countryside and Downtown Mount Prospect. During subzero January days, these older doors visibly bow inward. This bowing creates resistance in the tracks. Your opener must work harder to lift and lower the door. Over time, this extra strain damages opener components like drive gears, belts, and logic boards. Safety sensors can also misalign due to door flex. Regular winter stress leads to premature opener failure in many Mount Prospect garages. We understand these local conditions.

problemSigns.sign: Opener hums but the door doesn't move
problemSigns.detail: The opener motor runs, but the garage door remains stationary. This often points to a stripped gear.

problemSigns.sign: Door reverses before touching the floor
problemSigns.detail: The garage door starts to close, then stops and opens again. This can indicate misaligned safety sensors or an obstruction.
Your garage door remote controls or exterior keypad do not activate the opener, even with new batteries.
The photoelectric eyes at the bottom of the garage door track show blinking indicator lights, signaling an issue.

problemSigns.sign: Trolley moves but door stays down
problemSigns.detail: The opener's carriage moves along the rail, but the door remains closed. The trolley carriage may be broken or disconnected from the door.
